Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:3717

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi
 On The 3 rd Of February, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 13 of 2018
 Rajendra And Others
 Versus
 Savai Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Malviya - Advocate on behalf of Shri Romil
 Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the respondent No.3.
 Order

The present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant, challenging the award dated 25.09.2017, passed by the 10th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore, in Claim Case No.146/2016, whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim and awarded compensation amounting to Rs.4,49,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.

entities.text: 10th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factual matrix of the case is that on 19.01.2012, Neeraj Khandelwal, was driving his own car bearing registration No. MP-09-CA- 4548 from Ratlam to Indore, after attending a house-warming ceremony, via Badnawar.
The vehicle was being driven at a moderate speed.

When the car reached Amla Fata on Badnawar Road, the driver of the trailer bearing registration No. RJ-19-GB-8724,
respondent No. 2, was driving the said NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3717 2 MA-13-2018 vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and at an excessive speed.
While so driving, the trailer driver suddenly applied brakes without giving any signal or warning.
As a result, the car driven by Neeraj Khandelwal, which was following the trailer, collided with it and met with a severe accident.
In the said accident, Neeraj Khandelwal, Mrs. Sumitra, Mrs. Shashi, Ayush Khandelwal and Parth Khandelwal sustained grievous injuries and succumbed thereto.

The incident was reported at Police Station Badnagar, where a criminal case was registered against respondent No. 2,
the driver of the trailer, under Section 304-A of the IPC.
In the accident, deceased Mrs. Shashi Khandelwal, aged about 50 years, who was a housewife, also lost her life, thereby depriving the appellants of her love, care and affection.
The appellant/claimant being husband of deceased, filed a claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.17,00,000/-.

Learned claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.2 which was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.

Thus learned MACT after appreciating the evidence on record partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.4,49,000/- against the claim of Rs.17,00,000/-.
4.
The learned counsel for the appellant argued that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of deceased.
No amount under the head of future prospects has been awarded.
He prays for enhancement in the compensation.

5. Refutting the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3717 3 MA-13-2018 appellant, learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the finding arrived at by the learned tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court in this appeal.
6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. It is not in dispute that respondent No.2 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?
8. On perusal of impugned award, it appears that the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased as Rs. 3,000/- per month which should have been Rs. 4545/- as per Minimum Wages guidelines.
The claimants are also entitled for 10% future prospects.

The compensation amount is being reassessed as under :
Loss of dependency :
Annual Income : Rs. 54,540/-

Future Prospects (10%) : Rs 59,994/- Deduction (1/3) :
Rs 39.996/- Multiplier (9) : Rs. 3,59,964/- Consortium : 1,20,000/- Funeral Expenses : 15,000/- Loss of Estate : 15,000/-

Total Compensation : 5,09,964/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3717 4 MA-13-2018 9.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.

The claimants are entitled to get the enhanced sum of Rs. 60,964/- alongwith interest as has been awarded by the learned Tribunal subject to following conditions:-
i.
The respondent no.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against it.

ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee on the enhanced amount also, if required in the present case, within a period of 15 days from today.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE (ra)
